headline: Salt short Insurance Australia Group, viewing strong margin as an accounting illusion and valuation as stretched at 18x PE
reasoning: IAG rose 13.3% in February as analysts got excited about a strong insurance margin result. Salt viewed this margin as merely the result of a quota share arrangement where IAG paid away a portion of volume rather than a reinsurance premium, making it an accounting artefact rather than genuine improvement. On consensus forecasts IAG trades on forward PEs of 17.8x and 18.7x over the next two years, which Salt characterises as one of the world's most highly priced insurers.
quote: The fourth headwind was our valuation-based short in Insurance Australia (IAG, +13.3%). The result was solid and several analysts became excited by a very strong insurance margin, whereas we viewed this as merely being an outcome of a quota share arrangement that they had entered, where rather than paying away a reinsurance premium (and lowering their margin), they effectively paid away a portion of their volume instead. Consensus forecasts have IAG on forward PE ratios of 17.8x and 18.7x over the next two years, making it one of the world's most highly priced insurers.
